quest.title: The Trail of the God of Wisdom
quest.description: You and Paimon finally arrive at Sumeru City. Well, will you be able to get an audience with the Dendro Archon?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x700, Mora x27875, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

chapter.title: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Well, seems no matter which way we try, we can't find anything that'll lead us to Lesser Lord Kusanali. Hmm, guess our only choice now is to try meeting with the researcher that Tighnari recommended.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's from Sumeru and even has a position in the Akademiya. Maybe he'll be able to access more info from the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, are you Rohawi?

dialogues.speaker: Rohawi
dialogues.text: Yes, that's me. Can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! You see, Tighnari sent us here and...

dialogues.speaker: Rohawi
dialogues.text: What? Tighnari!?

dialogues.speaker: Rohawi
dialogues.text: Ah! Please, th—there's no need to say anything, really! Sure, I admit that the article I published last month wasn't my best work, and maybe the data didn't produce the most convincing results, but...

choices.text: Uh, I think you've misunderstood us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Here, this is a letter from Tighnari.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Oh, let me see... Ah, whew, what a relief! You two nearly scared the life out of me. So you two just have some questions for me?

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Seems even Tighnari acknowledges my innate ability for procuring information. So, what is it you two would like to know?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We want to meet with Lesser Lord Kusanali. Do you know a way we can do that?

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: You mean you want to meet the Dendro Archon herself? Uh, this isn't exactly my area of expertise, but let me see what I can find in the Akasha...

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Hmm, sorry, the Akasha didn't respond to my query.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, you too!? But what about your abilities for getting information and all that? *sigh* Paimon was sure you'd be able to access more info than we did.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Well, as I said, this isn't my area of expertise. I am but a lowly researcher, so the Akasha doesn't see a need for me to know more about the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: All I know is that ever since Lesser Lord Kusanali returned to Sumeru, she's never left the Sanctuary of Surasthana or made a public appearance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, didn't expect her to be such a mysterious figure.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: The Dendro Archon is somewhat of a recluse. Perhaps she just doesn't want to entertain visitors, which would explain the lack of information in the Akasha.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, but then what can we do?

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Heh, no need to worry just yet, I'm only hypothesizing here. You could certainly try asking around and see if anyone else has ideas.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: And besides, you two should consider the bright side of things. Not being able to see Lesser Lord Kusanali may not be a bad thing.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: In this world, there will always be information you cannot obtain from the Akasha, and things you can never accomplish. Knowing when to yield is a form of wisdom.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Take me, for example. It's a miracle if my brain cells can spit out one paper every three years... But Tighnari, that guy can publish three papers in just a single year.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, okay, thanks for your advice.

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Don't mention it. If you two ever want information about things like who's been promoted within the Akademiya or relations between The Six Great Sages, come find me.

choices.text: So by "area of expertise"...

response.speaker: Rohawi
response.text: Hey c'mon, this is a survival skill at the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Paimon's expectations were pretty low, but this is so low it's like digging holes in the dirt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what do we do now? Even if we want to talk to someone, we don't know anybody here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No, there's still one other person we know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Like who?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ad astra abyssosque.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you're right! Katheryne! The Adventurers' Guild has its own intel network. Let's hurry and find her.

choices.text: You meant this kind of stuff!?
We're not here to discuss academics.

talks.objective: Go to the Adventurers' Guild and ask Katheryne for help

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Ad astra abyssosque! Hello, Traveler and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Katheryne! We need your help with something.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Understood. The Adventurers' Guild is always ready to serve you. With what do you require assistance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We want to meet with Lesser Lord Kusanali. Do you know a way we can do that?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: You two wish to meet with Sumeru's archon. Understood. Please wait...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I apologize, but I am unable to call up any relevant information in the Akasha. I'm also unable to locate any pertinent information in my personal memory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, another dead end. Well, if Katheryne can't help us, then we really don't know anyone else to ask now...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Please do not worry. I may know of someone who can help you two.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: In Sumeru, the Adventurers' Guild does not serve as the vanguard of information. Rather, there are numerous active mercenary groups, collectively known as the Eremites.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: They take on various contracts and work all across Sumeru, so they naturally accrue intelligence.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: An Eremite brigade called the Corps of Thirty is in charge of Sumeru City's defenses. Not only are they the oldest brigade, but they are responsible for managing and coordinating the affairs of all other mercenary brigades.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Corps of Thirty? What a weird name...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Supposedly, they are named as such because their ranks numbered thirty at their inception.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Asfand, an adviser with the Corps of Thirty, maintains good relations with the Adventurers' Guild. Though he's already retired, he and his words carry great weight within mercenary circles.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: If you'd like to get in contact with him, you can find him at the Corps of Thirty's headquarters, the Citadel of Regzar.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks a bunch, Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: You're welcome. I wish you two the best of luck. We look forward to your exploits in Sumeru.

talks.objective: Go to the Citadel of Regzar and look for Asfand

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Welcome! The Adventurers' Guild told me to expect you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's nice to meet you, Asfand! We'd like to ask you about something.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain your reason for coming here...

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: I see. So Katheryne's the one who sent you this way.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Heh, it's true that the Eremites' network is vast, but even I can't help you meet the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, seriously? That's it?

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Haha, 'fraid so. The Eremites aren't terribly religious, so we don't know much about divinities. As far as the Akasha goes, we can access even less than you.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: We originally came from the desert — the gods there died off long ago. Since those days, we've used our own two hands to carve out a living. We don't beg gods for their aid.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: It isn't just us, though. If you ask me, I think most in Sumeru aren't interested in Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Just take the Akademiya for example. They're the ones who truly rule Sumeru. Although they believe in gods, most of 'em only care for the late Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: In their eyes, she was the one who founded Sumeru and gifted us with the Akasha. Lesser Lord Kusanali just happened to inherit her legacy.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Because of the Akademiya's influence, most citizens are more familiar with Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and hold her in greater esteem.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Not to mention that Lesser Lord Kusanali never makes an appearance, and the Akademiya never announces anything about her. As far as the people of Sumeru are concerned, she's just a god that exists... and that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Aw, after hearing all of that, Paimon sorta feels bad for Lesser Lord Kusanali...

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Hah, but who knows? We're all just guessing when it comes down to it. Besides, I'm sure the God of Wisdom doesn't worry about her reputation among people like us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, well thanks for the info, Asfand.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Haha, no problem. Always happy to help out the Adventurers' Guild.

talks.objective: Look for the young girl who has information about Lesser Lord Kusanali

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Seems Asfand was right about most people's attitudes here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not only are they not interested in the Dendro Archon, they even say stuff like, "If the Akasha doesn't think I should know, then I don't need to know about it."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've been asking for information non-stop ever since we got to Sumeru, but the harder we try, the more hopeless everything seems.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't there at least one person in this entire city who cares about Lesser Lord Kusanali?
Oh? You two are interested in Lesser Lord Kusanali?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you?
From the sound of it, you two are outlanders who recently arrived here. You've been asking around for information on Lesser Lord Kusanali, right?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I forgot to introduce myself. I am Dunyarzad, one of Lesser Lord Kusanali's faithful followers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, really? Then do you know how we can meet with her?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I can't help you with that, but your conversation earlier did happen to remind me of a legend about the Dendro Archon.

choices.text: What sort of legend?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Sure. It goes like this: Long, long ago, there was a man who heard a prophecy. It predicted that a great calamity was about to befall him.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Panicked by what he heard, the man sought out the Dendro Archon in the hopes that she would bless him with the wisdom to help him escape his predicament.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: The man journeyed across deserts and through rainforests, and experienced tribulations of every kind. However, he still couldn't find any trace of the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: In despair, he thought, "Alas, the Archon has abandoned me!" He then had no choice but to sorrowfully resign to his fate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... and then what happened?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: And then... the calamity came! But to his own surprise, the man felt somehow emboldened by the trials of his journey. By relying on his own strength, he managed to overcome the adversity.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: At that moment, a bird perched upon his shoulder. This bird was, in fact, an avatar of the Dendro Archon. She said:

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: "O archon-seeker, do you now understand? She and her wisdom have long been found by you."

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: "Along your journey, we were in every flower and blade of grass, every ray of sparkling sun, and every breath of dancing wind. So long as you continue to think and ponder, we'll be wherever you go."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What an amazing story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, thanks for the story. Paimon feels all warm and fuzzy inside after that!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hehe, in a way, it seems like this story is also one of the Dendro Archon's avatars.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunyarzad, since you worship Lesser Lord Kusanali, can you tell us anything else about her?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Of course! So, did you two know that...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Uh... Umm, I'm terribly sorry, but it seems something's come up now. Let's chat another day!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, wait! What the heck just happened?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think it has something to do with those people over there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks like they're searching for someone... Hmm, Dunyarzad was acting super nervous just now. You think they're looking for her?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This stinks! We finally managed to find a lead about Lesser Lord Kusanali. We can't let them get in the way now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's see if we can get rid of them. Then we can catch up with Dunyarzad!

choices.text: Can you tell us the legend?

talks.objective: Help Dunyarzad lure the pursuing mercenaries away

dialogues.speaker: Muruwa
dialogues.text: Hey, have you two seen a brown-haired girl wearing a purple top and a long blue dress? We're lookin' for her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did she have bandages wrapped around her wrists?

dialogues.speaker: Muruwa
dialogues.text: Yes, that's her! Did you see which direction she went?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah, she went that way!

dialogues.speaker: Muruwa
dialogues.text: Quick! After her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that should keep 'em busy for a while. Let's hurry and find Dunyarzad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you are, Dunyarzad! We thought you might've been long gone by now.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Ah! It's you two. You startled me there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can relax now, we threw those people looking for you off the trail.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Really? Oh, thank you so much! Unfortunately, I believe there are still more of them out there looking for me.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Uh oh, looks like there are some coming this way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? More of them!? Then what are we standing here for? Run!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: No, wait... I, uh... My body isn't in the best shape. It's difficult for me to run.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How about we find someplace to hide?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Okay, sounds good. There's a tavern on the other side of the port that we can go to. They probably wouldn't expect me to hide in a place like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's move out. Stay behind us, we'll keep an eye out for anyone looking for you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Whew, we made it. They shouldn't be able to find us now... Wait. Stand down, Dehya!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #My lady, who are {M#these two}{F#these two}?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: #{M#They}{F#They}'re travelers that I met on the street just a moment ago. They happened to notice that you all were searching for me, so they helped me hide.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I see. In that case, you two should scram. There's nothing here for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec, who the heck are you? And why are you shooing us away?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm Miss Dunyarzad's bodyguard, here to see that she returns home safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, let's get going. You've been gone for so long that your parents are worrying themselves sick.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: And if I refuse to go with you?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It'd be easier for the both of us if you cooperated, but if you insist on not going, then I'll have to carry you like a sack of potatoes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Dunyarzad already said she doesn't want to go back. Why are you still pushing her?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Stay out of this. You don't understand the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sorry, my lady. Even though I'm your bodyguard, your parents are my employers. I have to answer to them.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: ...How much?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait, what?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: How much Mora do I have to pay you to become your employer, so you never listen to my parents ever again? Double... Triple? Give me some time and I'll get that much!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, this isn't about Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *sigh* I don't know what you think of us Eremites, but let me say this: I like Mora, but I'll never go against my principles.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's why I'm here looking for you. Sure, it's an order from my employer, but my conscience was also telling me it's the right thing to do.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: And knowing your health, carelessly running around like this is gonna hurt ya. For the sake of those who love you, don't be stubborn.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: No, you're wrong! I'm aware of my limits, and I know what I'm doing. Honestly, the only people being stubborn right now are my parents.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: They know perfectly well that it makes no difference if I'm at home or not! They still won't accept reality!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: And every time I bring this up, they just change the subject. Dehya, you've been living with us a long time already. This should be old news to you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Dehya, I know it hasn't been easy for Mother and Father, and I'm grateful for everything they've done for me, but there is someone else in this world I'm also grateful to.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Because she saved me. The love I have for her is the same I have for my parents.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: This is my life and my last chance, so I want to do something meaningful!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, are you sure what you're doing now is meaningful?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Yes, I'm sure. At least... it is to me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fine, I won't ask you to return home anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But lemme make something very clear: I'm only doing this because I respect your determination, not because I agree with you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Thank you, Dehya! Sorry for being so rude just now. My nerves were acting up... And I even brought up your payment in such an offensive way...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it, my lady. I did say that I like Mora. Besides, that's our next topic of conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Today's little excursion caused such a ruckus that every single bodyguard at the estate was deployed. It won't be easy to hide things from your old man.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Since this definitely won't be your last escapade, here's a little tip... You should at least make it look like your room and things are still in order when you leave. Also, you'll need someone to cover for you when you're out and about.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So I'll let you hire me, my lady. This way, everyone wins. As for the pay... let's say half of what your father pays me. We can settle the bill when we return to the estate.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Okay, deal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, looks like they've reached an understanding.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm fine, really. I just feel a little tired now that things have calmed down...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, stop trying to look tough. We're already in a tavern, so let's rest up and grab some grub.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I'm sorry for worrying you two. If you don't mind, I'd like for you to join us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure! After you rest up, we wanna hear more about Lesser Lord Kusanali!

talks.objective: Rest in the tavern for a while

dialogues.speaker: Lambad
dialogues.text: Hah! Well, if it isn't Dehya! Haven't seen you in nearly half a year.

dialogues.speaker: Lambad
dialogues.text: Word on the street is that you are a bodyguard for the Homayani family now. Heh, don't you find that kind of work boring?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, you get used to it. How about a menu over here!

dialogues.speaker: Lambad
dialogues.text: You got it. Huh? Isn't this lil' Miss Homayani herself? Heh, we don't get to serve personages like you very often. We'll be sure to prepare our very best!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Thank you, sir, but there's no need. I don't have a lot of Mora on me, and I really ought to save as much as I can.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Ah, but please bring these two the best food you have. They're my new friends, so I want to be a good host for them.

choices.text: No need to break the bank, we'll eat whatever you order.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We're already super grateful for everything you told us about Lesser Lord Kusanali.

response.speaker: Lambad
response.text: How about our Charcoal-Baked Ajilenakh Cakes? They're our signature snack, and they run cheap. Look, other customers over there are eating some now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? They look kinda burnt and dry... Uh, Paimon will pass.

choices.text: Picky Paimon? Now that's a first...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, c'mon! Paimon has personal preferences too, you know!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After ordering, you continue chatting with Dunyarzad about Lesser Lord Kusanali...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunyarzad, we asked a lot of people when we first arrived, and almost nobody was interested in Lesser Lord Kusanali. So what made you want to follow her?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Well, remember when you asked me if I knew how to meet the Dendro Archon? Even though I don't know how, I think I've actually seen her before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, really?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yes, it was when I was a child. At that time, my illness had kept me bedridden for the better part of a year.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I was stuck inside and couldn't make any friends, and my parents did their best to find treatments for me... But even then, the Akasha didn't have any helpful information.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: My younger self no longer had any hopes or dreams. One flare-up was so bad that I was in a semi-conscious state for several days.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Then one night, I woke up alone in my room. I was terrified, my body was paralyzed. Even if I cried, there was no sound.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: At that moment, an ethereal voice spoke in my mind: "Dunyarzad, don't be scared. You don't have to cry."
Dunyarzad, don't be scared. You don't have to cry.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Huh? Who are you? How do you know my name?
Umm, how do I explain this... You might not be able to understand, but actually, I know everything about you.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Really?
Of course. I know that you're scared of thunder, that you hate taking medicine every morning, and that you love counting the petals on your mom's skirt.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Wow, you really do know everything.
Dunyarzad, is there anything you want?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Want? Not really... I can't go anywhere or do anything.
Huh? But aren't you a child? All children have wishes. Tell me what you want, and maybe I can make it happen.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Then... Can you make my illness go away?
Oh... I'm sorry, but I'm not powerful enough to do that right now...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Then... Can you be my friend?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: After that, the voice said, "Okay, I'll be your friend."

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Although my body was suffering during those days, that voice encouraged me and told me many wondrous things.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Beyond my window was the flourishing Sumeru City, beyond the city was a lush rainforest, and beyond that was the Wall of Samiel, deserts, and all of Teyvat...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Once I finally made it through that bout of illness, I couldn't hear the voice anymore. I told my mother about it, but she said that I must have been dreaming.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: But I know that that voice wasn't a figment of my imagination! Before that, I had never heard of "Teyvat."

choices.text: So you believe the voice you heard was...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yes, for sure!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: If it weren't for that voice, I would have never grown curious about the outside world, nor would I have learned how to read and enjoy so many books.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: That voice sparked a desire for wisdom — it had to have been the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I've been hoping for a chance to repay her kindness. In fact, I was running around today to help prepare the Sabzeruz Festival for her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's the Sabzeruz Festival?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It is Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday, which is the day that she was found by the sages.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It's actually an old holiday that originally celebrated Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's birthday. When she passed away, the holiday eventually became a celebration of the Lesser Lord's birthday.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I heard everyone was overjoyed when they welcomed her back to Sumeru. In those days, the festival was a huge deal.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: But because of the Akademiya's influence, people have gradually lost interest in the festival.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: The Akademiya actively participates in Sumeru's many holidays dedicated to Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, but when it comes to the Sabzeruz Festival, forget any funding, they practically act like it doesn't exist.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Maybe they see Lesser Lord Kusanali's birth as confirmation of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's death, so they're reluctant to celebrate it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, but that's awful!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: It is. It's absolutely terrible!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Sure, the Greater Lord founded Sumeru, but hasn't Lesser Lord Kusanali been the one quietly protecting us for the past few hundred years?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: *ahem* Just remember that we're still out in public. Don't get too carried away now...

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I know that people over by the Grand Bazaar still hold the Sabzeruz Festival to this day. But I hadn't met any of them before, so I was never able to contribute.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: But recently, I made a friend there who also follows Lesser Lord Kusanali!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I gave her my savings because I want her to throw a wonderful festival this year. That's the least I could do for Lesser Lord Kusanali.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hold on. My lady, does this friend happen to be Nilou? The one who sends flowers to the estate?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yes, that's her.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I saw her leaving the other day with a nervous look on her face, it seemed like she was hiding something in her arms. Did you give her something?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Ah, yes... Initially, I didn't have much Mora prepared, so I had Nilou sell one of my skirts.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: I've agreed with Nilou to meet up at the Grand Bazaar today and see how things are coming along. Dehya, would you accompany me?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Sure. That's quite the trip though — I'll carry you.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: No, that would be too much, even for you.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: You might as well just accept the lift. If I let you walk, who knows how long it'll take us! And if anything happens to you, then I'd really never hear the end of it from your father.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can we also come along?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: But of course! Nilou will be thrilled to hear that there are more people interested in Lesser Lord Kusanali.

choices.text: It was Lesser Lord Kusanali?
But you've cooked Slimes before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! What do you have against my Slime dishes?

choices.text: Don't worry about it. We'll pay for our own food.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, we're paying for ourselves now? Aww... Paimon kinda wanted to try something fancy, but we aren't exactly loaded. Guess Paimon will settle for something ordinary...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Think "Greater Lord Rukkhadevata."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Many bright dots of light appeared in my mind. I probably need to calm my mind and focus more to understand what they mean.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Feelings of affection, intimacy, nostalgia, sadness, and anxiety also come to my mind... These seem to be what the people of Sumeru feel about their departed archon.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh, Paimon's getting all teary-eyed all of a sudden... It feels like the people of Sumeru really miss their archon.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Sorry I'm late, Nilou.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh, Dunyarzad! It was taking you so long that I assumed you got trapped at home, but you made it in the end!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Uh oh, but if Dehya's here, that means you got caught, right?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: You could say that, but everything worked out! She's on our side now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hah, not completely.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Oh? And who are these two?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: #Oh, meet {NICKNAME} and Paimon, my two newest friends. They're visitors who just arrived at Sumeru City and are looking for information on Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: So you're followers from another land?

choices.text: Yep!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: That's wonderful! You two absolutely mustn't miss the Sabzeruz Festival!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: By the way, Dunyarzad, we've already started decorating the Grand Bazaar. It looks spectacular, thanks to your generous contribution!

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: You're very welcome! It's the only thing I could do. Do you still have enough Mora?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Uh, probably...? But don't sweat it. We've already finished renovating the stage! Come on, I'll show you.

choices.text: Truthfully, no.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Oh, really? Well, that's okay. You're still invited to the Sabzeruz Festival!

talks.objective: Go with Nilou to see the stage

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this place is amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Not bad. Heh, the last time I was here, the stairs were full of holes.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The stairs were nothing! A little while ago, we discovered that the tree above the stage had a huge chunk of bark ready to fall off. Mr. Zubayr was worried sick!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: We reported it to the Akademiya many times, but they never sent anyone to deal with it. We didn't want anything bad happening, so we were going to cancel all the stage performances.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why didn't anyone come to handle it?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, probably because it was the theater asking.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The Akademiya looks down on performers like us. They probably think it would be best if the theater closed down completely.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: We can't let that happen, though. Not only would everyone involved in the theater go hungry, but then we wouldn't be able to hold the Sabzeruz Festival anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Thank the Dendro Archon for Dunyarzad! With the Mora she gave us, we hired someone to patch up the tree, and we also gave the stage a much-needed makeover.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: The stage is going to be even prettier when it's festival time! I can't wait for you to see it!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: And I can't wait to see you on the stage! You've been practicing so long already — it's almost time for your dream to become reality!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: It's OUR dream! I'll do my best for the two of us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nilou, what are you gonna be doing at the festival?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: She'll be dancing the Dance of Sabzeruz, the most important performance at the Sabzeruz Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #Dunyarzad, have you told {M#them}{F#them} the origin of this holiday?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I only told them about the Greater Lord and Lesser Lord so far.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Okay, then I'll tell you two about how this holiday came to be...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: According to legend, the Sabzeruz Festival was originally the Goddess of Flowers' birthday celebration for the Greater Lord.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: A long, long time ago, on one of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's birthdays, her friends threw her a celebratory banquet.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Some of the gods got drunk. One started playing music and the Greater Lord started singing, so the Goddess of Flowers began to dance.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: As she danced upon the grass, countless beautiful Padisarahs began to bloom wherever she stepped.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Those brilliant purple flowers became her dazzling stage. All the gods clamored, "Oh, if only time could stop at this very moment."

choices.text: Sounds like they had a great time.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Of course they did! When people mention the gods, they always think of the Archon War, but Sumeru's gods also had happy times.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Although they aren't around anymore, they're preserved in our tradition of dance. This outfit I'm wearing is apparently based on how the Goddess of Flowers looked.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Though we're just tiny people compared to the divine, we still have to do our best to make sure that the birthday girl feels loved on her special day.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Nilou, you of all people will definitely be able to convey our well wishes to the Dendro Archon. I also noticed that you went the extra mile and scattered Padisarahs around the stage.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hehe, they symbolize the Goddess of Flowers after all. It's just a shame that all the real Padisarahs went extinct after her death.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yeah. The Greater Lord brought forth Padisarahs in memory of the Goddess of Flowers, but she ultimately could never truly replicate that beautiful purple.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Thinking about the Goddess of Flowers' dance makes me wish I could've seen it.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: If my stage were anything like that... *sigh* I'd be thrilled if I had just two real Padisarahs on the stage.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: So Traveler and Paimon, what do you think? Interested in the Sabzeruz Festival? Will you two be coming?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: All of Lesser Lord Kusanali's followers will be there for her birthday. It'll be a good opportunity for you to learn more about her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon thinks that's a great idea!

choices.text: You sure it's not because you want in on the fun?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey c'mon, there's nothing wrong with enjoying a festival! Besides, it's Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday. She'll be happy to have more people who are celebrating it.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Hehe, so how about we all attend the Sabzeruz Festival together?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like a plan!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Dunyarzad, let me show you which stage decorations we've picked out so far. Traveler and Paimon, if that doesn't sound interesting to you, then feel free to explore the area.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Everyone at the Grand Bazaar loves Lesser Lord Kusanali, and we're all looking forward to the Sabzeruz Festival.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, we'll take a look around.

choices.text: You sure it's not because you want to watch Nilou dance?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course Paimon wants to watch! Those two things aren't mutually exclusive, you know.

choices.text: That sounds somewhat bittersweet.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Huh, really? Oh, you probably mean because all the gods in this story are no longer alive.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Nilou, your outfit looks amazing. There's also something different about you from when we first met up.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hehe, I thought I'd add little extra pizzazz to my dress for the festival. See?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Wow, did you sew all that yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Uh-huh, sewing is a fundamental skill for everyone in the theater company because we make all our own costumes. Did you know that Mr. Zubayr not only can make costumes, but props too?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hehe, I've noticed that you can't keep your eyes off this crown. Would you like to try it on?

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh, may I?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Of course! The legends say that the Goddess of Flowers had beautiful horns on her head, so this crown was made to reflect that. Ah, Dunyarzad! You look absolutely stunning with it on! It's like I'm looking at the Goddess of Flowers herself...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Revamping the stage for the festival couldn't have been easy, that's for sure. I bet this year's festival will be one to remember.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I don't know much about the Grand Bazaar, but I do know that the residents here have a penchant for song and dance... Heh, two things that the Akademiya doesn't particularly approve of.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, and the perfume sold around here is a lot better than what you'll find elsewhere. The fragrances are longer-lasting, and they're gentler on your skin...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Uh, I mean... that's what I've heard, at least!

dialogues.speaker: Kumari
dialogues.text: Whoa, what's with your yellow hair? And why do your clothes look so funny? Are you an outlander?

dialogues.speaker: Kumari
dialogues.text: Did you know that the Sabzeruz Festival is about to happen? There'll be loads of fun things to do at the festival, but the best part is when Farris, the Knight of Flowers, passes out candy to everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Shrimati
dialogues.text: Ah, dancing at the Sabzeruz Festival. You know, I also danced when I was younger.

dialogues.speaker: Shrimati
dialogues.text: As a child, I even asked my grandmother why we performed the dance for the Lesser Lord when it was originally done to honor the Greater Lord.

dialogues.speaker: Shrimati
dialogues.text: My grandmother said that Greater Lord Rukkhadevata is a beloved deity and honored by all, and Lesser Lord Kusanali is too. If the Goddess of Flowers ever knew Lesser Lord Kusanali, then she would certainly have wished to be her friend and hold celebrations for her, too!

dialogues.speaker: Shrimati
dialogues.text: The Sabzeruz Festival has been losing its appeal over the years... That is, until a wealthy benefactor stepped in this year and brought the festival back to life. I heard she forked out a lot of Mora to make it all happen.

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: Things are really shaping up, and there's a buzz around the festival this year. We're expecting people from all over to come by this year and buy things during the festivities.

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: Don't be fooled into thinking that Sumeru City has the best of everything. Some festival snacks are only offered here in the Grand Bazaar.

dialogues.speaker: Farhad
dialogues.text: And when it comes to musicians, dancers, or singers, the Grand Bazaar's got the best of the best! Sure, those folks at the Akademiya might not like it, but what's a festival without song and dance?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm late. It took some convincing for the master and mistress to believe that Miss Dunyarzad was only sitting in the port for a while because she was in a bad mood.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Anyway, I guess I should be thanking you. I haven't seen Miss Dunyarzad that happy in a long time. If wasn't for you two, she probably would've been caught and dragged back much earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure sound a whole lot nicer than when we first met, Dehya. Who would've thought you had such a soft spot for Dunyarzad?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Tch, it's called being a professional. I'm a bodyguard, and I work for whoever's paying.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, look! Dehya's blushing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep, that's a blush if I've ever seen one.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ugh! Listen, you two...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I don't expect to be working for Miss Dunyarzad very long, but I hope to finish things on a positive note if possible... Let's cut the chitchat and head into the Citadel. We'll see if the person I know has a way for you two to meet with the Lesser Lord.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, heya Chief!

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Ah, Dehya! What're you doing here? And well, well, didn't expect to see you three together.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hah! I take it you all know each other already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! We met this morning after the Adventurers' Guild pointed us to Asfand for more info.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: No kidding... So where's Rukh Shah? I thought I'd help these two out by asking about the theft. Anything you can tell 'em?

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Rukh Shah's gone over to the Akademiya. The Grand Sage recently ordered Sumeru City to begin bolstering its defenses, so people from all over have been called back to the city.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Ahem, since you've already mentioned the theft, I suppose I might as well tell 'em what we know.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Appreciate it, Chief!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, theft?... Sorry, what the heck are you guys talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just recently, the Akademiya lost something... and there's a chance the item is connected with the Dendro Archon. This case might just somehow help you in meeting her.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Heh, I suppose that's one way to look at it, but if ya ask me, the case is more about the Akademiya than anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Lemme fill ya in. The Akademiya recently sent a convoy to pick up an important package from Aaru Village. Word got out, and the convoy was robbed on its way back.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: The Grand Sage took the whole matter very seriously. Not only did he dispatch the matra, but also enlisted our help in the search for leads. All we know so far is that whatever was stolen is currently in Port Ormos.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You two have heard of Port Ormos, haven't ya? It's the largest commercial port in all of Sumeru. You can travel there by leaving Sumeru City and heading south along the river.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The Akademiya's grip isn't long enough to reach all the way to Port Ormos, so the city's a little more laid back, meaning the population's also a mixed bag. You never know who you'll meet there.

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: Apparently, what was lost has a great deal to do with the Akasha, knowledge, and even the gods. I'm afraid I don't have any other details for ya, though...

dialogues.speaker: Asfand
dialogues.text: If you're interested, maybe you could head to Port Ormos and ask around yourselves. If you want my advice, try introducing yourselves as students of the Akademiya once you're there.

choices.text: Huh? Students of the Akademiya?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Are ya serious, Chief? All the Akademiya students are in Sumeru City, you know... Why should they pretend to be students in Port Ormos?

response.speaker: Asfand
response.text: Heh, if you're all so interested, just go there and see what happens!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Count me out. I've got plenty of work to do here for the Homayani family.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: And take it from me: If you two really do decide to visit Port Ormos, you'd best watch your backs. Let's just say that the Eremites there aren't nearly as friendly as those here in Sumeru City.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: There are even some extremists who go around shouting slogans like "Retake Sumeru for King Deshret!" Word is that more and more are joining their movement. They're becoming a real headache for Chief and the others.

response.speaker: Asfand
response.text: You bet they are. *sigh* King Deshret's been dead for thousands of years. Now they start spreading rumors of his return. Ridiculous!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Not everyone's like you, Chief. Even the desert natives who abandoned their homes in the wilderness still wish to have a god of their own.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, that's about all the information we have for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks, Dehya! And you too, Asfand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since we've gathered all we could for the moment in Sumeru City, let's head to Port Ormos and see what we can find next.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Miss Dunyarzad is looking forward to seeing you both at the Sabzeruz Festival, so be sure to get yourselves back here in time for that.

choices.text: Yep, we won't forget.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Good. Then we'll see you both at the Sabzeruz Festival.

choices.text: Don't worry, we will.
Why should we do that?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After leaving the Citadel of Regzar, you question several people in Sumeru City...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, is that who Paimon thinks it is? It looks like... Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: ♪ *hums* ♪

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, come to think of it, Paimon's only ever seen her behind the counter at the Adventurers' Guild... This is the first time we've ever seen her taking a break.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, hey, it's the Traveler and Paimon. What's shakin'?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, break time Katheryne sure sounds a lot less formal than usual. Paimon was still waiting for her to say "ad astra abyssosque"!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Sure, standing behind the counter at the Adventurers' Guild doesn't require any complicated functions.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: But saying and doing the same old things over and over again can get pretty monotonous, like watching the same Fontaine movie day after day.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: But take you two for example. You travel across Teyvat to enrich your lives and gain new experiences.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, we enjoy traveling across Teyvat and all that, but we're mainly looking for clues about {M#his sister}{F#her brother}.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Yes, and you should keep searching. Sometimes the answers we're looking for aren't necessarily at our intended destination. Instead, they're found along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, haven't we heard someone say something pretty similar recently? Anyways, what brings you out here, Katheryne?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you also a fan of the Sabzeruz Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: No, not particularly, I guess you could say that I'm loving the recent atmosphere here. If festivals bring happiness to everyone, then that's where their true value lies.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Oh, it looks like it's about time for me to be heading back now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we'll see you next time at the Adventurers' Guild! Oh, by the way, thanks for connecting us with the Eremites. We've already made some great friends in Sumeru City thanks to you!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I'm sure you two will get along well with the people here. You've already been blessed by the element of Dendro, after all. See ya around!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, there's something really different about Katheryne today...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, Traveler, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh hey, Dehya. What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I've got something to tell ya. My lady knows you're looking for ways to meet Lesser Lord Kusanali, and she's been trying to come up with a way to help you. Well, I have an idea that might help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you serious? We'd love that!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It might not necessarily pan out, so don't get your hopes up too much. I'll need to take you two somewhere and ask someone some questions.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about Dunyarzad?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady is feeling a little worn out at the moment. Nilou's found a place for her to rest. After I take my lady home, let's meet in front of the Citadel of Regzar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a plan!

talks.objective: Go to the entrance of the Citadel of Regzar to wait for Dehya

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sumeru City! Ah, we finally made it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, did you see that? When those people entered the city, something on their heads lit up!

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: One moment please, you two. It appears this is your first time visiting Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Yeah, that's right, but how did you know that?

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: Because there's currently no information on either of you in the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: But no need to worry, that won't prevent you from entering the city. In fact, the Akademiya conveniently provides each traveler to Sumeru City with a device.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: Perhaps you two have heard of the Akasha before. It's our beloved Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's lasting legacy, a treasure trove of collected knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: After centuries of tireless research on the Akasha, the Akademiya created one of its most ingenious inventions, the Akasha Terminal.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: As long as you are within Sumeru's borders, you may use an Akasha Terminal to connect directly to the Akasha and access any knowledge you need.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: I should mention that due to technical limitations, the operation of Akasha Terminals will be much smoother and more effective in large cities such as Sumeru City and Port Ormos.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so this is the thing that Tighnari was telling us about. It sounds pretty amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: You two are quite fortunate. Until recently, it was standard practice to only issue Akasha Terminals to outlanders who spent an extended amount of time in Sumeru. However, this policy was recently changed, and now all travelers are issued one upon arrival.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: Here are your Akasha Terminals. Please handle them with care.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, it kinda looks like a leaf.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: To activate it, simply hold it in your hand and say the following phrase to yourself: "May the Mighty God bless us with their voice of wisdom."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, since this little doodad lets you access knowledge, maybe we can use it to find a way to meet Lesser Lord Kusanali. Let's give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: May the Mighty God bless us with their voice of wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem! May the Mighty God bless us with their voice of wisdom...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Just now, something clicked and Paimon suddenly knew how to use this thing! It seems all we need to do is concentrate on what we wanna know... and BAM! You get it! Ohh, that'll come in real handy!

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: Exactly. That is the power of the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Panah
dialogues.text: And with that, let me officially welcome you both to Sumeru City. May the wisdom of the Dendro Archon always be your guide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, now that we're in, we can check the Akasha about Lesser Lord Kusanali. Let Paimon try...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, the sages found a newly born deity from within some scorched ruins... The deity now resides in the Sanctuary of Surasthana... Hmm, seems pretty similar to what Collei was telling us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, next, let's concentrate on asking how to meet her... Huh? Paimon doesn't sense anything... Hmm, the Akasha didn't respond to Paimon's question.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh, the same happened to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, c'mon! Ugh, focusing on this question feels like when you have something you're trying to remember and it's on the tip of your tongue, but you just can't think of it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon's brain is exhausted...

choices.text: I'll try asking the Akasha something else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, smart idea! But what are you going to ask it?

choices.text: Maybe I'll indirectly find more information about Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Think "Why doesn't the Akasha answer my question?"

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A vague thought suddenly comes to mind... The Akasha doesn't unconditionally respond to every query.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Also, even if the same query is requested by multiple people, the Akasha still imparts knowledge based on each person's identity, age, experiences, and other demographics.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, could it be because we're outlanders and we've only just arrived in Sumeru? You know, maybe we're not qualified to receive an answer to this sort of question or something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Think "Lesser Lord Kusanali."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Some knowledge began to trickle into my mind for a moment, but there wasn't really anything that I didn't already know.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, you too? Well, glad it's not just Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Muruwa
dialogues.text: Strange. Where did she go? She couldn't have made it far.

dialogues.speaker: Hamasa
dialogues.text: There's no way we can return to the master and mistress empty-handed. I'll ask around again.

dialogues.speaker: Sharaf
dialogues.text: Excuse me, sir. Have you seen a brown-haired girl wearing a purple top and a long blue dress?

dialogues.speaker: Aftab
dialogues.text: Eh? What did you say? ...Oh, yes, I have a granddaughter!

dialogues.speaker: Sharaf
dialogues.text: I wasn't asking about your granddaughter. I asked if you had seen a young woman go by!

dialogues.speaker: Aftab
dialogues.text: Ah yes, she and her parents settled down in Port Ormos... I haven't seen her in a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Sharaf
dialogues.text: Eh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see, Tighnari wrote an address on the letter's envelope... Oh, it's not far from the city's gate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's head over and have a look. Hopefully he's at home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, off to the Citadel of Regzar we go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's head over to the Citadel of Regzar and wait for Dehya.
